In the main model, acceptance implies a device signature or a leaked device key, a relay countersignature over exactly that observation and signature or a leaked relay key, and, for device-attested data that the device never signed, the leak of both keys; the legacy branch is reachable only for declared legacy devices; injective agreement fails because exact replays are accepted by the cryptographic layer. In the variant with an attacker-writable device-to-gateway link the device key alone suffices. \texttt{formal/rule\_l\_bounded\_check.py} checks Rule L exhaustively for one device, one epoch, sequence numbers 0--3 and at most two contents per slot: 1,060,190 (admitted set, order) pairs on a re-implementation over the real registry (3,540,885 when \textsf{prev} may also be null), and all 390,024 orders of the standard sets (3,425,892 receipts) on the unmodified verifier with real signatures; 0 violations of order independence, contest monotonicity, contest of equivocation and gap-fill with an arriving successor, and duplicate idempotence (\texttt{results/formal/rule\_l\_bounded\_check.log}). In 553 of the 1,088 admitted sets a forged alternative remains authoritative: exactly those in which neither the genuine content nor its genuine successor was admitted.
